We need to design the full architecture for a distributed caching system. The system must support multi-region replication, automatic failover, TTL-based eviction, and a pluggable backend. Document the component breakdown, the data flow from client to cache to backend store, the consistency model, the failure modes, and the operational runbook for cache warm-up after a regional outage.

Draft a new observability plan for the routing service that covers structured logging standards, metric cardinality budgets, alerting thresholds for the bandit reward signal, and a sampling strategy for the decision log that keeps storage costs below fifty dollars per month while preserving enough fidelity to run post-incident analyses on routing anomalies.

Design the team conventions for Mahoraga v2 routing decision documentation. The conventions must specify the mandatory fields from the decision log, the escalation path for reward signal anomalies, the ownership model for each bandit component, the minimum acceptance criteria for a v3 arm before reaching live traffic, and a sign-off checklist capturing both technical and operational readiness before any new arm enters the active roster.

We need a comprehensive incident response plan for when the Ollama service becomes unavailable during business hours. The plan should include detection criteria, immediate fallback behavior when no arms are available, stakeholder communication templates for different incident severities, a decision tree for when to escalate versus attempting automated recovery, and a post-mortem template capturing the routing state at the time of the outage.

Outline the migration path from the v1 keyword router to the v2 per-bucket LinUCB bandit for a team relying on the v1 routing decisions database. The plan must address bootstrapping the v2 bandit state from v1 observations, the validation criteria confirming the migration is stable, the rollback procedure if v2 mean rewards drop below the v1 baseline for more than three consecutive days, and the sign-off gates at each migration phase.

We need to plan the rollout of a new multi-region deployment for the orchestration service. The deployment must handle traffic shifting across three availability zones, include a staged canary release covering five percent of traffic before full promotion, and provide a rollback procedure that restores the previous version in under ten minutes with validated health checks at each stage before proceeding.
